title: RAH Release Compliance Report
description: Validates instances of compliance/release-compliance-report.json — the formal engineering record produced by the Release Validator after evaluating a Release against Release Contract 1.0. Not a deployment report, not a qualification report, not an installation log (4. Stage 4...md Sec 7.1-7.2). Immutable once generated; if the Release changes, a completely new validation cycle runs (Sec 7.10). Neither the Offline Platform nor the Offline Qualification Procedure shall modify this report (Sec 7.12).

generator_version.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 9.21, Sec 8.14: 'Generator version where available' — the only version field in this schema that is explicitly optional, since a Compliance Report can in principle be produced by re-validating an existing Release without the original Generator being available.

validator_version.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 7.5, Sec 9.21, Sec 8.14. A Validator update must not silently change what a given rule means for an already-frozen Release (Sec 9.23).

release_identity.description: COMPLETED — Sec 9.21 requires 'Release identity' in the report but does not enumerate its sub-fields; these three are the minimum needed to unambiguously identify which Release this report covers, matching the identity fields used elsewhere in the Contract (release-manifest.schema.json#/application/slug, #/release/version, and the Release fingerprint referenced in PackagingResult, 4.6...md Sec 6.6).

validation_environment.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 9.21 ('validation environment'). Free-text/identifier describing where validation ran (e.g. Packager runtime version and OS).

overall_result.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 7.7. Only PASS/FAIL are permitted; no ambiguous or partially-successful overall state (Sec 9.2). PASS = every mandatory validation rule succeeded. FAIL = at least one mandatory validation rule failed.

rules_not_applicable.description: COMPLETED — not in the Sec 7.9 minimal list, but NOT_APPLICABLE is a defined outcome state (Sec 9.8) and Sec 9.21 requires the report to include not-applicable explanations, so a count is included for completeness.

rules_not_executed.description: COMPLETED — same reasoning as rules_not_applicable, for the NOT_EXECUTED outcome state.

rules.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 7.6 canonical example, Sec 7.8 required per-rule fields, Sec 9.21 fuller list (adds not-applicable/not-executed explanations).

id.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 7.8. Corresponds to an id in validation-rules.json, e.g. RC-DIR-001. COMPLETED: category-code length varies (RC-DB is 2 letters, RC-REPRO is 5), so the pattern below is deliberately wider than a fixed 3 letters — matches every category actually declared in validation-rules.json#/categories.

category.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 7.6 example. One of the categories declared in validation-rules.json#/categories.

message.description: EXTRACTED — Sec 7.8 ('human-readable explanation'). For NOT_APPLICABLE, states why the rule's trigger condition did not apply. For NOT_EXECUTED, states which earlier fatal failure prevented evaluation. Sec 9.17: shall never print a complete secret value here.

$comment: Deliberately-omitted fields, recorded so a future session doesn't silently re-add them without a Contract version bump. severity: named only as a possible FUTURE field in Sec 7.8 ('optional future fields explicitly deferred, not in v1: execution duration; severity; supporting evidence') — deliberately absent from Contract 1.0. operator / who-validated identity: no such field exists anywhere in the architecture's Compliance Report description — the process is described as fully deterministic/automated with no human-operator-identity field. If an audit trail by person is ever needed, that is a MINOR-or-later Contract addition, not an omission to silently fix now.
